vllm._comment: Optional — defaults for auto-generated vLLM profiles. image overrides the stock vllm/vllm-openai tag; image_gpt_oss overrides the gpt-oss image. Set moe_backend to "" to omit --moe-backend entirely and let vLLM autoselect (recommended on GB10/sm_121, where the Marlin MoE kernel miscomputes for some architectures).
vllm._comment_serve: serve_command is normally omitted — it is derived from the image, because whether an explicit 'vllm serve' is needed is a property of the image's entrypoint, not of the model. vllm-openai images serve on entrypoint (derives to ""); images that exec their arguments, such as eugr/spark-vllm, need 'vllm serve'. Set explicitly to override, including "" to add nothing.

llamacpp._comment: Optional — the GGUF quant ladder. One profile script covers a whole repo's quants, so the quant/ctx/spec choice is data the UI enumerates and passes as RECIPE, not a script per combination. vram_gb is what admission checks, so keep it honest.
llamacpp._comment_spec: spec: embedded = the NextN/MTP head baked into the target GGUF, works on a stock build. fastmtp = a separate sidecar GGUF, which needs fastmtp_image — an image built from the release patch. Verified 2026-08-20: the stock upstream image rejects the sidecar (expected 5120, 248320, got 5120, 32768), so the patched build is genuinely required.

balanced.desc: Default. Near-Q8 quality, holds up on tool-calling.

coexist.desc: Fits beside a large vLLM model. Run both engines at once.

longctx.desc: Max native context. KV dominates; vision off for headroom.

paths._comment: vllm_scripts and llamacpp_scripts are where generated profile scripts are written and scanned from; relative paths resolve against $HOME.

litellm_k8s._comment: Optional — describes a LiteLLM that runs in Kubernetes off a configmap instead of a systemd unit. With enabled true, a config change syncs paths.litellm_config into the configmap and rolls the deployment, because the pod mounts the configmap read-only and a file write alone is invisible to the cluster. All keys optional — omit the section (or set enabled false) to restart the systemd unit instead; namespace defaults to "default", configmap to "litellm-config", configmap_key to "config.yaml", deployment to "litellm".

alerts._comment: All keys optional — omit this section entirely to keep defaults. webhook_url falls back to the DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL env var; interval_s falls back to ALERT_CHECK_INTERVAL.

sites_discovery._comment: The Dashboards tab finds running web UIs itself: every non-loopback TCP listener plus every Kubernetes NodePort gets one HTTP GET, and a port earns a card only if it answers with an HTML page. Ports answering JSON/plain text are kept as kind=api behind a toggle. All keys optional.
sites_discovery._comment_exclude_services: exclude_services suppresses a Kubernetes-discovered card by "namespace/name" (or a bare name, matching in any namespace) instead of by port number, so it survives a NodePort reassignment and does not blacklist an unrelated future service that happens to reuse that port.

homelab._comment: Optional — the node list for System > Homelab (the built-in default lists this author's four machines, so set your own). tailscale_ip is optional; leave it out for a node that is not on the tailnet.

hosts._comment: Optional — name the machines you link to from the Dashboards tab once, so a sites entry can say "host": "controlplane" instead of repeating an IP everywhere it's used. Values are a hostname or IP only (no scheme, no port).

sites._comment: Optional overlay on discovery, not the list itself. An entry with a port renames/describes/groups that discovered port (curation beats the page's <title>). An entry with a verbatim url pins something discovery cannot see — a UI on another host. An entry with a host names a machine from the top-level hosts map and is always pinned, never overlaid, because its port belongs to that machine and not to this one. Ports resolve against the entry's host → app.sites_base → app.host → the request host; scheme defaults to http. Configured entries stay visible even when down, so a dashboard you care about never silently disappears.

sites.name: Cluster Console
sites.desc: Runs on the control-plane node, not this box
